title: 2 Kings Chapter 19 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Kings chapter 19 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Kings Chapter 19 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Kings Chapter 19.

questions.question: What did King Hezekiah do when he heard the news?
options: He rent his clothes and covered himself with sackcloth
He built a wall around the city
questions.correctAnswer: He rent his clothes and covered himself with sackcloth
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 19:1 states that when King Hezekiah heard it, he rent his clothes and covered himself with sackcloth.

questions.question: Who did King Hezekiah send to Isaiah the prophet?
options: Eliakim, Shebna, and the elders of the priests
questions.correctAnswer: Eliakim, Shebna, and the elders of the priests
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 19:2 says Hezekiah sent Eliakim, Shebna, and the elders of the priests to Isaiah.

questions.question: How did Hezekiah describe the day in his message to Isaiah?
options: A day of trouble, rebuke, and blasphemy
A day of joy and celebration
A day of peace and rest
A day of harvest and plenty
questions.correctAnswer: A day of trouble, rebuke, and blasphemy
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 19:3 states Hezekiah said, 'This day is a day of trouble, and of rebuke, and blasphemy.'

questions.question: What did Hezekiah ask Isaiah to do for the remnant left?
questions.correctAnswer: Lift up his prayer
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 19:4 indicates that Hezekiah asked Isaiah to lift up prayer for the remnant that are left.

questions.question: How did Isaiah respond to Hezekiah's servants?
options: Be not afraid of the words of the Assyrian servants
questions.correctAnswer: Be not afraid of the words of the Assyrian servants
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 19:6 records Isaiah telling them not to be afraid of the words with which the Assyrian servants have blasphemed God.

questions.question: What did Isaiah say the LORD would send upon the king of Assyria?
options: A blast that causes him to hear a rumor and return home
questions.correctAnswer: A blast that causes him to hear a rumor and return home
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 19:7 states the LORD will send a blast upon him causing him to hear a rumor and return to his own land.

questions.question: Where was the king of Assyria warring when Rabshakeh returned to him?
questions.correctAnswer: Libnah
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 19:8 says Rabshakeh found the king of Assyria warring against Libnah.

questions.question: Who was said to have come out to fight against the king of Assyria?
questions.correctAnswer: Tirhakah king of Ethiopia
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 19:9 mentions Tirhakah king of Ethiopia coming out to fight against the king of Assyria.

questions.question: What did the messengers from the king of Assyria tell Hezekiah about his God?
options: Let not thy God deceive thee
Thy God is stronger than Assyria
questions.correctAnswer: Let not thy God deceive thee
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 19:10 records the message telling Hezekiah not to let his God deceive him.

questions.question: According to the message from Assyria, what had the kings of Assyria done to all lands?
questions.correctAnswer: Destroyed them utterly
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 19:11 states the kings of Assyria had destroyed all lands utterly.

questions.question: Which of the following cities or places was NOT mentioned in the kings of Assyria's message?
questions.correctAnswer: Jerusalem
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 19:12 lists Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and Eden in Thelasar but not Jerusalem.

questions.question: True or False: Hezekiah went up into the house of the LORD and spread the letter before the LORD.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 19:14 confirms Hezekiah went into the house of the LORD and spread the letter before Him.

questions.question: True or False: The servants of King Hezekiah came to Isaiah while wearing fine garments.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 19:2 states the servants were covered with sackcloth, not fine garments.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah assured that God would cause the king of Assyria to fall by the sword in his own land.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 19:7 records Isaiah saying God will cause him to fall by the sword in his own land.

questions.question: True or False: Rabshakeh remained in Jerusalem to negotiate peace with Hezekiah.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 19:8 shows Rabshakeh returned to the king of Assyria who was warring against Libnah, not staying to negotiate.

medium.title: 2 Kings Chapter 19 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Kings Chapter 19 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Hezekiah do after receiving the letter from the messengers?
options: He tore his clothes and prayed in the temple
He read the letter and went into the house of the LORD to spread it before Him
He immediately sent a reply to the king of Assyria
He gathered his army to prepare for battle
questions.correctAnswer: He read the letter and went into the house of the LORD to spread it before Him
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 19:14 states that Hezekiah received the letter, read it, and then went up into the house of the LORD and spread it before the LORD, showing his trust and dependence on God rather than immediate military action or retaliation.

questions.question: In Hezekiah's prayer, how does he describe God?
options: As a warrior who fights for Israel
As the God dwelling between the cherubims, the only God of all kingdoms who made heaven and earth
As a distant God who watches over Israel
As a god among many in the kingdoms of the earth
questions.correctAnswer: As the God dwelling between the cherubims, the only God of all kingdoms who made heaven and earth
questions.explanation: In 2 Kings 19:15, Hezekiah prays acknowledging God as the God of Israel who dwells between the cherubims and the sole Creator and ruler over all kingdoms, emphasizing God's sovereignty and unique position.

questions.question: What specific request does Hezekiah make to the LORD in his prayer regarding Sennacherib's words?
options: To hear and see the reproach against the living God and save them
To grant him victory in battle without divine intervention
To allow peace negotiations with Assyria
questions.correctAnswer: To hear and see the reproach against the living God and save them
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 19:16-19 shows Hezekiah asking God to listen and look upon the reproachful words of Sennacherib and to save them so that all kingdoms know God alone is LORD, showing faith in God's deliverance and a desire for His glory.

questions.question: According to Hezekiah's prayer, what have the kings of Assyria done to the nations and their gods?
options: They have made allies with the gods
They have destroyed the nations and cast their gods into the fire because those gods were man-made idols
They have spared the gods but destroyed the lands
They have worshipped the gods of the nations
questions.correctAnswer: They have destroyed the nations and cast their gods into the fire because those gods were man-made idols
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 19:17-18 states that the Assyrian kings destroyed nations and their lands and cast their gods—wood and stone made by men's hands—into the fire, showing the futility of idol worship compared to the living God.

questions.question: What reason does Hezekiah give for asking God to save them from the hand of Sennacherib?
options: So they can expand their kingdom
So all the kingdoms of the earth may know that the LORD God is the only true God
So they can collect tribute from Assyria
questions.correctAnswer: So all the kingdoms of the earth may know that the LORD God is the only true God
questions.explanation: In 2 Kings 19:19, Hezekiah prays for deliverance so that all kingdoms will recognize the LORD God as the only true God, highlighting the desire for God's glory through their salvation.

questions.question: What message did Isaiah send to Hezekiah in response to his prayer?
options: That God had rejected his prayer
That God had heard his prayer against Sennacherib
That Hezekiah must prepare for war
That Hezekiah should surrender to Assyria
questions.correctAnswer: That God had heard his prayer against Sennacherib
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 19:20 explicitly states that Isaiah sent word to Hezekiah that the LORD God of Israel has heard his prayer against Sennacherib, indicating God's attentiveness and involvement.

questions.question: How is the 'daughter of Zion' described in relation to Sennacherib?
options: She despised and laughed him to scorn
questions.correctAnswer: She despised and laughed him to scorn
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 19:21 describes the daughter of Zion as despising Sennacherib and laughing him to scorn, showing confidence in God's protection despite the Assyrian threat.

questions.question: According to God's message through Isaiah, against whom has Sennacherib exalted his voice and blasphemed?
questions.correctAnswer: The Holy One of Israel
questions.explanation: In 2 Kings 19:22, God points out that Sennacherib has reproached and blasphemed against the Holy One of Israel, showing the personal nature of the offense against God Himself.

questions.question: What boast does Sennacherib make through his messengers, according to 2 Kings 19:23?
options: That he will make peace with Jerusalem
That he will conquer the mountains and forests including the sides of Lebanon and Carmel
That he fears the God of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: That he will conquer the mountains and forests including the sides of Lebanon and Carmel
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 19:23 records Sennacherib's boast of coming with many chariots to cut down tall cedars of Lebanon and enter the lodgings of borders and forests, demonstrating his arrogance and confidence in military might.

questions.question: What does Sennacherib claim to have done to the water sources of besieged places?
options: He has dug and drunk strange waters and dried up rivers with his feet
He has supplied them with fresh water
questions.correctAnswer: He has dug and drunk strange waters and dried up rivers with his feet
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 19:24 shows Sennacherib boasting about digging and drinking strange waters and drying up all rivers of besieged places with the sole of his feet, emphasizing his claim of complete dominance.

questions.question: What does God remind Sennacherib about His power and past acts in verse 25?
options: That God has formed and laid waste fenced cities from ancient times
That the gods of nations are stronger
questions.correctAnswer: That God has formed and laid waste fenced cities from ancient times
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 19:25 reminds Sennacherib that God formed the lands long ago and brought to pass the laying waste of fenced cities, asserting God's sovereign power over history and nations.

questions.question: How does God describe the inhabitants of the cities destroyed by Assyria in verse 26?
options: Small in power, dismayed, and like grass or corn blasted before growing
questions.correctAnswer: Small in power, dismayed, and like grass or corn blasted before growing
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 19:26 describes the inhabitants as weak and frightened, comparing them to grass on the field or rooftop and corn blasted before growing, highlighting their vulnerability against Assyria.

questions.question: What does God promise to do because of Sennacherib's rage and tumult as stated in verse 28?
options: Put a hook in his nose and a bridle in his lips to turn him back the way he came
questions.correctAnswer: Put a hook in his nose and a bridle in his lips to turn him back the way he came
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 19:28 promises divine intervention to restrain Sennacherib by putting a hook in his nose and bridle in his lips, forcing him to retreat the way he came, symbolizing God's control over arrogance.

questions.question: What sign does God give about the agricultural conditions for the next three years in verse 29?
options: Famine will destroy all crops for three years
They will eat what grows by itself the first year, what springs the second, and sow and reap the third
questions.correctAnswer: They will eat what grows by itself the first year, what springs the second, and sow and reap the third
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 19:29 describes a sign of God's provision: eating naturally grown food the first year, then newly sprouted crops the second, and finally sowing and reaping in the third, indicating restoration and hope.

questions.question: How does this passage teach about faith and trust in God during times of crisis?
options: To rely on military strength alone
To pray and seek God’s help, trusting in His sovereignty and power over nations
To negotiate with enemies for peace
To ignore threats and do nothing
questions.correctAnswer: To pray and seek God’s help, trusting in His sovereignty and power over nations
questions.explanation: Hezekiah’s actions (2 Kings 19:14-19) show that faith involves prayer and reliance on God's protection, recognizing His power over all kingdoms and trusting Him in crisis rather than human strength.

hard.title: 2 Kings Chapter 19 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Kings Chapter 19.

questions.question: What does the LORD say He will put in the king of Assyria's nose and lips to turn him back?
questions.correctAnswer: A hook and a bridle
questions.explanation: Verse 2 Kings 19:28 states that because of the king's rage, the LORD will put 'my hook in thy nose, and my bridle in thy lips, and I will turn thee back by the way by which thou camest.' This symbolizes divine control and humiliation.

questions.question: According to the LORD's sign to Hezekiah, when will the people be able to sow and reap vineyards again after the siege?
questions.correctAnswer: In the third year
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 19:29 reveals the sign: 'in the third year sow ye, and reap, and plant vineyards, and eat the fruits thereof,' indicating restoration after hardship.

questions.question: What is promised to the remnant that escapes from the house of Judah?
options: They shall take root downward and bear fruit upward
They shall be scattered among the nations
They shall build a great army
questions.correctAnswer: They shall take root downward and bear fruit upward
questions.explanation: Verse 2 Kings 19:30 promises that the remnant will 'take root downward, and bear fruit upward,' symbolizing growth and restoration after calamity.

questions.question: What will the zeal of the LORD of hosts accomplish according to 2 Kings 19:31?
options: Bring forth a remnant from Jerusalem and Mount Zion
questions.correctAnswer: Bring forth a remnant from Jerusalem and Mount Zion
questions.explanation: The verse states that 'the zeal of the LORD of hosts shall do this' by bringing forth a remnant from Jerusalem and Mount Zion, emphasizing divine preservation.

questions.question: What does the LORD declare the king of Assyria will NOT do to Jerusalem?
options: Come into the city, shoot an arrow, come before it with shield, or cast a bank against it
Lay siege for more than a year
questions.correctAnswer: Come into the city, shoot an arrow, come before it with shield, or cast a bank against it
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 19:32 clearly states the LORD's protection: the king 'shall not come into this city, nor shoot an arrow there, nor come before it with shield, nor cast a bank against it.'

questions.question: How will the king of Assyria return from Jerusalem according to the LORD's word?
options: By the way that he came
He will not return at all
questions.correctAnswer: By the way that he came
questions.explanation: Verse 2 Kings 19:33 states that the king 'by the way that he came, by the same shall he return,' indicating defeat and retreat.

questions.question: For whose sake does the LORD promise to defend Jerusalem?
options: For His own sake and for His servant David's sake
For the sake of the priests
For the sake of the temple treasures
questions.correctAnswer: For His own sake and for His servant David's sake
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 19:34 reveals God's motivation: 'For I will defend this city, to save it, for mine own sake, and for my servant David's sake,' emphasizing covenant faithfulness.

questions.question: How many Assyrian soldiers did the angel of the LORD smite in one night?
questions.correctAnswer: One hundred eighty-five thousand
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 19:35 describes that 'the angel of the LORD went out, and smote in the camp of the Assyrians an hundred fourscore and five thousand,' a miraculous deliverance.

questions.question: What happened to Sennacherib after the LORD's judgment on his army?
options: He departed, returned, and dwelt at Nineveh
questions.correctAnswer: He departed, returned, and dwelt at Nineveh
questions.explanation: Verse 2 Kings 19:36 states that 'Sennacherib king of Assyria departed, and went and returned, and dwelt at Nineveh,' marking the failure of his campaign.

questions.question: Who killed Sennacherib and where was he worshipping at the time?
options: His sons Adrammelech and Sharezer killed him while he was worshipping in the house of Nisroch
He was killed by Hezekiah in the temple
He was assassinated by Babylonian spies
questions.correctAnswer: His sons Adrammelech and Sharezer killed him while he was worshipping in the house of Nisroch
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 19:37 explains that 'as he was worshipping in the house of Nisroch his god, that Adrammelech and Sharezer his sons smote him with the sword.'

questions.question: Which other Old Testament book contains a prophetic account similar to the LORD putting a 'hook in the nose' of a king to control him?
questions.correctAnswer: Isaiah 37
questions.explanation: Isaiah 37 parallels 2 Kings 19, recounting the same event and divine intervention against Sennacherib, including the imagery of a hook in the nose (Isaiah 37:29).

questions.question: What is the Hebrew meaning of the word 'remnant' as used in 2 Kings 19:30, and how does it reflect the theme of this chapter?
options: A surviving group preserved by God, symbolizing hope amidst judgment
A large army ready for battle
questions.correctAnswer: A surviving group preserved by God, symbolizing hope amidst judgment
questions.explanation: The Hebrew term for 'remnant' (שְׁאֵרִית, she'erit) refers to survivors preserved by God. This reflects the theme of restoration and divine protection in this chapter (2 Kings 19:30).

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in the passage from 2 Kings 19:22-25 where the LORD recounts past deeds and challenges the king of Assyria?
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasm
questions.explanation: Verses 22-25 use chiasm, a literary device where ideas are presented and then repeated in reverse order to emphasize God's sovereignty and past acts, framing the king's arrogance.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD's defense of Jerusalem was solely for Hezekiah's sake according to 2 Kings 19.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 19:34 states the LORD will defend Jerusalem 'for mine own sake, and for my servant David's sake,' not solely for Hezekiah, showing God's covenant faithfulness.

questions.question: True or False: The destruction of the Assyrian army by the angel of the LORD occurred overnight.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 19:35 describes that 'that night, the angel of the LORD went out, and smote in the camp of the Assyrians an hundred fourscore and five thousand,' confirming the overnight event.

theological.title: 2 Kings Chapter 19 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Kings Chapter 19 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What was King Hezekiah's initial reaction upon hearing the threat from the king of Assyria?
options: He rent his clothes and went into the house of the LORD
He immediately sent soldiers to battle
questions.correctAnswer: He rent his clothes and went into the house of the LORD
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 19:1 shows that upon hearing the threat, Hezekiah rent his clothes, covered himself with sackcloth, and went into the house of the LORD, demonstrating mourning and seeking God in crisis.

questions.question: Which leaders did Hezekiah send to Isaiah the prophet to seek guidance during the crisis?
options: Eliakim, Shebna, and the elders of the priests
questions.correctAnswer: Eliakim, Shebna, and the elders of the priests
questions.explanation: According to 2 Kings 19:2, Hezekiah sent Eliakim, who was over the household, Shebna the scribe, and elders of the priests to Isaiah to seek God's counsel.

questions.question: What does Hezekiah's prayer in 2 Kings 19:15-19 reveal about his understanding of God's uniqueness?
options: God is the only true God who made heaven and earth and dwells between the cherubims
God is one among many gods of the earth
God is distant and uninvolved in earthly affairs
God's power is limited compared to Assyrian gods
questions.correctAnswer: God is the only true God who made heaven and earth and dwells between the cherubims
questions.explanation: Hezekiah's prayer in verses 15-19 emphasizes God's unique sovereignty as the creator and the only true God, dwelling between the cherubims, affirming monotheism and God's transcendence.

questions.question: What divine attribute is demonstrated by God's promise to defend Jerusalem 'for mine own sake, and for my servant David's sake'?
questions.correctAnswer: Faithfulness to covenant promises
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 19:34 shows God's faithfulness to His covenant with David, indicating His steadfast loyalty and commitment to His promises.

questions.question: How does the narrative of Sennacherib's defeat in 2 Kings 19:35-36 connect to the broader redemptive story of Israel?
options: It demonstrates God's protection of His covenant people against foreign powers
It marks the end of Israel's monarchy
It reveals the failure of prayer
questions.correctAnswer: It demonstrates God's protection of His covenant people against foreign powers
questions.explanation: The defeat of Sennacherib in verses 35-36 illustrates God's sovereign intervention to protect Jerusalem, affirming His role as protector of His covenant people throughout redemptive history.

questions.question: What theological theme is expressed in Isaiah's message to Hezekiah that 'The virgin the daughter of Zion hath despised thee, and laughed thee to scorn'?
options: The assured victory of God's people despite threats
The neutrality of Jerusalem in conflict
The triumph of Assyria over Israel
questions.correctAnswer: The assured victory of God's people despite threats
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 19:21 conveys God's assurance that despite Assyria's threats, Jerusalem (the daughter of Zion) will triumph, reflecting God's protective sovereignty.

questions.question: According to 2 Kings 19:28, what metaphor does God use to describe His control over Sennacherib's rage?
options: A hook in the nose and a bridle in the lips
A wall of fire around Jerusalem
A shield to protect the city
questions.correctAnswer: A hook in the nose and a bridle in the lips
questions.explanation: Verse 28 uses the metaphor of putting a hook in the nose and a bridle in the lips to symbolize God's sovereign control over Sennacherib's rage and actions.

questions.question: What doctrine about the nature of idols is taught in Hezekiah's prayer (2 Kings 19:18)?
options: Idols are mere works of men's hands and not true gods
Idols are manifestations of the true God
questions.correctAnswer: Idols are mere works of men's hands and not true gods
questions.explanation: In verse 18, Hezekiah prays that the gods of other nations are wood and stone made by men, thus not true gods, affirming the biblical doctrine of the futility of idolatry.

questions.question: What combined teaching do 2 Kings 19:6 and 2 Kings 19:11 provide about trusting God in the face of blasphemy?
options: Believers must not fear blasphemous threats because God is sovereign and able to deliver
God is indifferent to insults against Him
Trusting God guarantees immediate worldly victory
Blasphemy against God is acceptable in times of war
questions.correctAnswer: Believers must not fear blasphemous threats because God is sovereign and able to deliver
questions.explanation: Verse 6 commands Hezekiah not to fear Assyria's blasphemy, and verse 11 reminds that God's power surpasses worldly destruction, teaching trust in God's sovereignty amid reproach.

questions.question: How does 2 Kings 19:29-30 illustrate the doctrine of restoration after judgment?
options: A remnant will take root again and bear fruit after a period of desolation
Israel will be permanently scattered without hope
questions.correctAnswer: A remnant will take root again and bear fruit after a period of desolation
questions.explanation: Verses 29-30 indicate that after hardship, a remnant of Judah will be restored, symbolizing God's faithfulness to renew and preserve His people post-judgment.

questions.question: What attribute of God is highlighted by His declaration that He 'formed' the lands and brings to pass their destruction as in verse 25?
options: God's sovereignty over creation and history
God's mercy in sparing all nations
God's impartiality to good and evil
questions.correctAnswer: God's sovereignty over creation and history
questions.explanation: Verse 25 reveals God's sovereign control over the formation and destruction of nations, affirming His ultimate authority over all history and creation.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God's protection of Jerusalem in 2 Kings 19 is merely political coincidence. What does 2 Kings 19:34-35 actually teach about God's intervention?
options: God miraculously defends the city by sending an angel to destroy the Assyrian army
The city was saved through superior military tactics
The Assyrians withdrew due to drought
The city was never truly threatened
questions.correctAnswer: God miraculously defends the city by sending an angel to destroy the Assyrian army
questions.explanation: Verses 34-35 describe that God Himself defends Jerusalem by sending His angel to strike down 185,000 Assyrian soldiers, showing divine supernatural intervention beyond human means.

questions.question: What does the message in verses 22-24 teach about God's holiness and the folly of human pride?
options: God is the Holy One of Israel, and human pride in opposing Him leads to vain boasting and judgment
God tolerates human arrogance without consequence
Human pride can rival God's power
God is silent in the face of blasphemy
questions.correctAnswer: God is the Holy One of Israel, and human pride in opposing Him leads to vain boasting and judgment
questions.explanation: Verses 22-24 show that Sennacherib's blasphemy against the Holy One of Israel is futile pride, which God confronts, teaching His holiness and the error of human arrogance.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about prayer is taught by Hezekiah’s actions and Isaiah’s response in verses 2-7?
options: Prayer in times of crisis invites divine assurance and intervention
Prayer is unnecessary when facing political threats
God does not hear prayers of kings
questions.correctAnswer: Prayer in times of crisis invites divine assurance and intervention
questions.explanation: Hezekiah sends messengers to Isaiah to pray, and Isaiah delivers God’s reassuring message in verses 2-7, teaching that God hears and responds to prayer in crises.

questions.question: How do verses 30-31 reveal God's redemptive plan through the concept of a remnant?
options: God preserves a faithful remnant from Jerusalem to fulfill His promises
All will be destroyed without exception
The remnant is left to political alliances only
questions.correctAnswer: God preserves a faithful remnant from Jerusalem to fulfill His promises
questions.explanation: Verses 30-31 emphasize God's sovereign preservation of a remnant from Jerusalem and Mount Zion, underscoring the biblical theme of remnant theology in redemption.
